content: The test image shows a tomato field with plants severely wilted/collapsed across the entire plant, leaves still appearing green. The pattern suggests a vascular wilt disease causing sudden, whole-plant collapse. Now I'll view one reference image to confirm my top candidate.

The reference image for Bacterial_Wilt shows a stem cross-section with bacterial streaming in water (diagnostic test), not the same field presentation as the test image.

**Analysis of test image:**
- Whole-plant collapse/wilting across multiple tomato plants in rows
- Leaves still green (no yellowing or necrosis) — indicates rapid vascular blockage, not foliar disease
- Staked commercial tomatoes on raised beds with white plastic mulch (typical southeastern US production)
- Some plants completely flattened, others partially wilted — classic patchy field distribution of soil-borne wilt pathogen
- Bugwood ID 1568047

This pattern strongly points to **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (Ralstonia solanacearum) — the rapid green wilt affecting whole plants, the southeastern US commercial production setting with plastic mulch, and the patchy distribution across rows are all hallmark features of this disease.
